item.title: In Seoul, 'Ruling Party Victory' and 'Opposition Party Victory' Tied at 40% Each... Democratic Party 'Nervous', People Power 'Hopeful' (서울서 ‘여당 승리’ ‘야당 승리’ 40% 동률…민주 ‘긴장’ 국힘 ‘기대’)
item.description:
On the 15th, 19 days before the June 3 local elections, the ruling and opposition parties were stirred by the results of a Gallup Korea poll on the outlook for the local elections. (6·3 지방선거가 19일 앞으로 다가온 15일. 여야는 지방선거 결과 전망에 관한 한국갤럽 여론조사 결과를 두고 술렁였다.)

In a survey conducted by Gallup Korea from the 12th to the 14th targeting 1,011 eligible voters aged 18 and older nationwide (with a margin of error of ±3.1 percentage points at a 95% confidence level, via mobile phone virtual number telephone interviews) regarding President Lee's job performance evaluation, 44% responded that 'many ruling party candidates should be elected,' while 33% said 'many opposition party candidates should be elected,' marking an 11 percentage point difference. Compared to similar polls in March and April, where the response 'many ruling party candidates should be elected' averaged about 17 percentage points higher than 'many opposition party candidates should be elected,' the gap has significantly narrowed. <<> In particular, in Seoul, the response that 'ruling party candidates should be elected' and 'opposition party candidates should be elected' were both at 40%. In a survey two weeks ago, the 'ruling party candidate should be elected' response was 8 percentage points higher, but the gap has now disappeared. <<> Democratic Party 'Nervous'... People Power 'Hopeful' <<> The two parties showed contrasting reactions. The Democratic Party responded that it would closely monitor support trends. A Democratic Party lawmaker assisting in the regional governor elections in the Yeongnam area said, “With less than 20 days left until the election, we need to stay alert,” adding, “As we enter the official campaign period from next week, if the gap narrows further in next week’s polls, the Democratic Party will have to consider its options.” Democratic Party Secretary-General Cho Seung-rae stated at a parliamentary press briefing, “We expected the support gap to narrow significantly, and it actually came later than we anticipated,” adding, “It doesn’t seem that the public's structural perceptions—such as the nature of local elections and attitudes toward each party—have changed. We will carry out our election campaign to ensure these structural perceptions translate into votes.” <<> The People Power Party appears encouraged. <<> A party leadership official said, “It’s true that the atmosphere has shifted due to the combination of the push for a special counsel to withdraw prosecutions, rising real estate prices, and the assassination attempt,” adding, “If we continue this momentum and emphasize the stability of incumbent regional governors, we can win back not only conservatives but also the moderates.” Within the party, expectations and concerns are mixed. A lawmaker from the Seoul metropolitan area noted, “As the true face of candidate Jung Won-oh is being revealed, combined with the push for a special counsel to withdraw prosecutions, the conservative rallying momentum is extending even to Seoul,” but warned, “At times like this, we should adopt a humble approach, but I’m concerned that Representative Jang Dong-hyuk’s assertive and abrasive style might backfire.” A lawmaker from the Yeongnam region said, “As the election nears, there’s a clear sense of conservative consolidation, with the feeling that we can’t hand over even Yeongnam to the Democratic Party,” but added, “The key is whether the conservative rally can spread to Chungcheong, Gangwon, and the metropolitan area.” <<> 44% Oppose, 27% Favor Granting Special Counsel Authority to Withdraw Prosecutions <<> Meanwhile, in this Gallup poll, 44% of respondents said that the special counsel investigating alleged fabricated prosecutions should not be granted the authority to withdraw indictments. 27% responded that the special counsel should be granted the authority to withdraw indictments, while 28% remained undecided. <<> By party affiliation, 43% of Democratic Party supporters favored granting the authority to withdraw prosecutions, while 27% opposed it. Conversely, among People Power Party supporters, opposition (68%) far outweighed support (14%). Among unaffiliated voters, opposition (50%) also significantly exceeded support (12%). <<> By political orientation, among those who identified as moderate, opposition (45%) outweighed support (27%). Among those who positively evaluated President Lee’s job performance, support for granting the authority to withdraw prosecutions (39%) and opposition (30%) were not far apart. <<> By region, opposition to granting the authority to withdraw prosecutions prevailed in most areas. In terms of support and opposition by region, the results were as follows: Seoul (27% support, 44% opposition), Incheon/Gyeonggi (24% support, 49% opposition), Daejeon/Sejong/Chungcheong (26% support, 44% opposition), Daegu/North Gyeongsang (25% support, 51% opposition), and Busan/Ulsan/South Gyeongsang (20% support, 49% opposition). Even in Gwangju/Jeolla (35% support, 39% opposition), where Democratic Party support is strong, the support and opposition rates were within the margin of error. <<> Presidential Approval Rating at 61%… Two Weeks Ago It Was 64% <<> In the Gallup poll, President Lee Jae-myung’s approval rating was 61%, while the disapproval rating was 28%. In the same survey two weeks ago, the approval rating was 64%, and the disapproval rating was 26%. Reasons for the positive evaluation included the economy/livelihoods (26%), diplomacy (10%), overall good performance (7%), communication (6%), and job competence/ability (6%). A Gallup official analyzed, “Economic issues are at the top of the list when it comes to reasons for a positive presidential evaluation,” adding, “The KOSPI, which has been surging over the past few months, approached the 8000 mark this week, and South Korea’s market capitalization has risen to 6th place in the world.” <<> On the other hand, reasons for the negative evaluation included ethical issues/avoidance of personal trials (10%), excessive welfare/livelihood subsidies (10%), the economy/livelihoods/high exchange rates (9%), overall poor performance (8%), real estate policy (7%), and dictatorship/arbitrariness (7%). Compared to two weeks ago (from the 28th to the 30th of last month), mentions of ethical issues among the reasons for disapproval have increased. The Gallup official analyzed, “This seems to be influenced by the controversy over granting the authority to withdraw prosecutions to the ‘Special Counsel for Investigating the Yoon Suk Yeol Regime’s Alleged Fabricated Prosecutions’ (fabricated prosecution special counsel), which the ruling party is pushing for.” <<> Professor Shin Yool of Myongji University (Political Science and Diplomacy) commented on the ‘excessive welfare’ criticism, saying, “The impact of Policy Planning Director Kim Yong-beom’s remarks on the ‘National Dividend’ has been significant. Although President Lee Jae-myung stepped in and called it fake news, the initial shock was so great that even the president’s claims seemed insufficient to quell the fire,” adding, “It’s also clear that the issue of the special counsel’s authority to withdraw prosecutions has had a very significant impact.” <<> The Democratic Party proposed the fabricated prosecution special counsel bill on the 30th of last month. The bill sparked controversy by including provisions allowing the special counsel to withdraw indictments in cases such as the alleged preferential treatment in the Daejang-dong development project. After President Lee requested a period of deliberation on the fabricated prosecution special counsel bill, the Democratic Party agreed to discuss the timing, procedures, and content of the bill after the local elections. <<> For more details, refer to the Gallup and the National Election Survey Deliberation Commission websites. <<> Reporter Jo Hee-yeon choh@hani.co.kr Reporter Jang Na-rae wing@hani.co.kr Reporter Kim Chae-woon cwk@hani.co.kr (한국갤럽이 지난 12일부터 14일까지 전국 만 18세 이상 유권자 1011명을 대상으로 실시한 이 대통령 국정수행 평가 조사(표본오차는 95% 신뢰 수준에서 ±3.1%포인트, 휴대전화 가상번호 전화 인터뷰) 결과 ‘여당 후보가 많이 당선돼야 한다’는 답변은 44%, ‘야당 후보가 많이 당선돼야 한다’는 응답은 33%로 11% 포인트 차였다. 3∼4월 같은 조사에서는 ‘여당 후보가 많이 당선돼야 한다’는 응답이 ‘야당 후보가 많이 당선돼야 한다’는 응답보다 평균 17% 포인트 가량 웃돌았던 것에 견주면 격차가 크게 준 것으로 나타난 셈이다.)

item.title: Han Dong-hoon’s ‘Prosecutor’s True Colors’ Rival Yoon Suk-yeol…First Deny, Then ‘Shut Their Mouth’ [Nonsseol] (윤석열 뺨치는 한동훈 ‘검사본색’…일단 부인하고 ‘입틀막’ [논썰])
item.description:
Hello. This is Lee Jae-sung from Nonsseol. (안녕하세요. 논썰의 이재성입니다.)

Han Dong-hoon, an independent candidate running in the by-election for the Busan Buk-gu Gap National Assembly seat, is struggling with a ‘cold-blooded’ image. On the 9th (Saturday), at his candidacy press conference, he began his speech without any particular reaction after seeing a broadcast cameraman filming him fall off the stage, sparking controversy. (부산 북구갑 국회의원 보궐선거에 출마한 한동훈 무소속 후보가 ‘냉혈한’ 이미지로 곤욕을 치르고 있습니다. 지난 9일(토요일) 출마 기자회견장에서 자신을 촬영하던 방송사 영상기자가 무대 밖으로 떨어지는 걸 보고도 별다른 반응 없이 연설을 시작해 논란이 된 건데요.)

The cameraman was filming Candidate Han as he approached the stage, but when Han came toward him with his back turned, the cameraman stepped back to secure distance and fell off. Candidate Han turned his head to look at the source of the noise. He then leaned in once more to get a closer look, then pulled the speech script from his pocket as if nothing had happened. The reactions of those around him, who rushed over to check on the fallen cameraman, stood in stark contrast to Han’s seemingly indifferent behavior. Criticism followed, such as “He didn’t even act surprised, let alone worried,” and “He just stared and didn’t move a muscle.” (해당 영상기자는 무대 위로 올라오는 한 후보를 촬영하던 중, 한 후보가 등을 진 채 다가오자 거리를 확보하기 위해 뒤로 물러서다 아래로 떨어졌습니다. 한 후보는 고개를 돌려 소음의 진원지를 쳐다봅니다. 그리고 몸을 한 차례 더 기울여 자세히 들여다본 뒤, 별일 없었다는 듯 주머니에서 연설 원고를 꺼냅니다. 추락한 기자의 상태를 살피려 우르르 몰려들었던 주변 사람들의 반응과 한 후보의 무신경해 보이는 행동은 확연히 대조됩니다. “걱정은커녕 놀라는 척도 안 한다” “쳐다만 보고 미동도 안 한다” 등의 비판이 잇따랐습니다.)

It’s possible he misjudged the situation momentarily due to the crowd and noise, or he might have passed it over thoughtlessly, eager to finish his speech quickly. If so, he could have just offered a sincere apology. But the next day, Candidate Han’s camp released this statement: (사람이 많고 소란해 순간적으로 판단을 잘못했을 수도 있고, 얼른 연설을 마쳐야 한다는 생각에 무심코 지나쳤을 수도 있습니다. 그렇다면 진솔하게 사과하면 됩니다. 하지만 한 후보 캠프는 다음날 이렇게 밝혔습니다.)

“Preliminary candidate Han Dong-hoon was not aware that the reporter fell, and this is sufficiently verifiable in the footage.” (“한동훈 예비후보는 해당 기자분이 넘어지는 것을 인지하지 못했으며, 이는 영상에서 충분히 확인 가능합니다.”)

This is an absurd and ridiculous response. Anyone with normal perception would inevitably judge from the footage that Candidate Han must have been aware of the situation, yet they interpreted it in the exact opposite way. First, Yoon Suk-yeol’s ‘Biden-nalimyeon’ tested the nation’s hearing, and now this is a vision test? The notice ends like this: (어처구니없고 황당한 대응입니다. 정상적인 지각을 가진 사람이라면 누구나 한 후보가 이 상황을 인지하지 못했을 리 없다고 판단할 수밖에 없는 영상을 정반대로 해석했습니다. ‘바이든-날리면’으로 국민 청력 테스트하던 윤석열에 이어 이번엔 시력 테스트입니까? 해당 공지문은 이렇게 마무리됩니다.)

“Malicious dissemination of false information during the election period is subject to severe punishment. We inform you that legal action will be taken against malicious dissemination of false information.” (“선거기간 악의적인 허위사실 유포는 엄벌 대상입니다. 악의적인 허위사실 유포에 대해서는 법적 조치 예정임을 알려드립니다.”)

Even the ‘shutting their mouth’ resembles Yoon Suk-yeol. No wonder they’re birds of a feather, and he was called ‘Yoon Suk-yeol’s crown prince.’ (‘입틀막’까지 윤석열과 닮았습니다. 괜히 유유상종이고, ‘윤석열의 황태자’였겠습니까?)

Former People Power Party spokesperson Park Sang-soo: The first video posted was extremely malicious. It made it look like Han Dong-hoon stayed still while watching someone fall. But looking at footage from various angles released accurately later, since the fall happened behind his back, it’s an angle where you simply couldn’t know unless you had eyes in the back of your head or superpowers. So this was such a clear case of false information dissemination that we decided to respond. (May 11, TV Chosun) (박상수 전 국민의힘 대변인: 처음에 올린 영상이 굉장히 악의적이에요. 한동훈 대표가 넘어지는 걸 보면서도 가만히 있었던 것처럼 이렇게 되거든요. 근데 여러 각도에서 지금 다른 각도에서 정확하게 나온 영상들을 보면 등 뒤에서 넘어졌기 때문에 이게 등에 눈이 있거나 초능력이 없으면 도저히 알 수가 없는 각도입니다. 그래서 너무나 명백한 허위 사실 유포라서 그냥 이거는 대응을 하기로 했습니다. (5월 11일 TV조선))

Since it happened behind his back, he naturally couldn’t see the fall itself. Who said he saw the fall directly? The criticism is about Candidate Han’s post-incident handling. The claim that he didn’t notice the worried crowd gathering and murmuring is a near-false excuse. Yet lawyer Park Sang-soo sets up a straw man by arguing that Han couldn’t have seen the fall, so why attack him as if he did? Truly a remarkable ‘legal trickster’ technique. (등 뒤에서 벌어진 일이므로 추락 장면 자체는 당연히 볼 수가 없죠. 누가 추락 장면을 직접 봤다고 했습니까? 비판의 대상은 한 후보의 사후 대처입니다. 사람들이 걱정스레 몰려들어 웅성거리는 상황을 인지하지 못했다는 말은 거짓에 가까운 변명입니다. 그런데 박상수 변호사는 한 후보가 추락 장면을 보지 못했는데 왜 봤다고 공격하느냐며 허수아비를 때립니다. 참으로 놀라운 ‘법꾸라지’ 기술입니다.)

As the controversy persisted, Candidate Han personally addressed it on the 12th (Tuesday). (논란이 이어지자 지난 12일(화요일) 한 후보가 직접 나섰습니다.)

Independent candidate Han Dong-hoon: I saw our spokesperson lying there like that. So I asked, ‘Hey, what’s wrong?’ I asked the spokesperson... ‘Are you okay?’ Looked like it was okay. So I moved on. But still, I wasn’t aware of the situation at all at that moment, but he came to film my event well. Oh, but it doesn’t seem he was hurt badly. We checked. Still, it was a close call. Oh dear. In that sense, I feel sorry about it. (May 12, KNN NEWS) (한동훈 무소속 후보: 우리 대변인이 이렇게 넘어져 있더라고. 그래서 어 왜 그러냐? 대변인에게 물어봤는데 (…) 괜찮냐? 보니까 괜찮다. 그래서 제가 넘어갔던 건데. 그래도 이게 뭐 저는 그 당시 상황은 인지는 전혀 못 했습니다만, 아 그래도 (…) 제 행사를 잘 찍어 주시려고 오신 거잖아요. 아이고 근데 많이 다치시거나 그런 거 같진 않아요. 저희가 연락해 보니까요. 그렇지만 그래도 아유 좀 큰일 날 뻔했다. 아이고. 어, 그런 점에서는 제가 아, 그 좀 저 죄송스럽게 생각한다는 마음이 있어요.” (5월 12일 KNN NEWS))

What exactly is he sorry for? He didn’t know the situation, but still, the person came to film him, wasn’t hurt badly, but it was a close call so he’s sorry? People are asking why he pretended not to notice, but he evades with the difficult phrase of not being aware and then talks about the reporter’s well-being. This is a classic Han Dong-hoon-style diversion. Moreover, checking various versions of the footage, there’s no scene of Han speaking to his spokesperson. It’s covering a lie with another lie. (대체 뭐가 죄송하다는 말일까요? 자신은 당시 상황을 몰랐지만, 그래도 자길 찍어주려고 온 분인데, 많이 다치지는 않았지만, 큰일 날 뻔 해서 죄송하다? 사람들은 왜 모른 척했느냐 묻고 있는데, 상황을 인지하지 못햇다는 어려운 표현으로 빠져나가며, 기자의 안부를 말합니다. 전형적인 한동훈식 논점 이탈인데요. 게다가 여러 버전의 영상을 찾아봐도 한 후보가 대변인에게 말을 거는 장면은 보이지 않습니다. 거짓을 거짓으로 덮는 꼴입니다.)

Furthermore, Han Dong-hoon’s camp says they will take legal action against those who spread the video, but the initial footage from the accident day was posted on the YouTube channel ‘Han Dong-hoon.’ Is he saying he’ll take legal action against himself? What could have ended with an admission and apology is now snowballing. (더구나 한동훈 캠프가 영상 유포자에 대해 법적 대응을 하겠다는데, 제일 처음에 보신 사고 당일 영상은 유튜브 ‘한동훈’ 채널에 올라온 영상입니다. 본인이 본인에 대해 법적으로 대응하겠다는 말인가요? 그냥 인정하고 사과하면 끝났을 일이 일파만파 커집니다.)

People Power Party lawmaker Kwon Young-se said this: (권영세 국민의힘 의원은 이렇게 말했습니다.)

“People rushing over when someone falls would have created noise, so I think it’s unlikely he didn’t know. (…) In Han Dong-hoon’s case, even if he saw it, he should have admitted things like ‘I was thoughtless’ right away. Saying he didn’t see it is a dishonest attitude.” (May 12, Channel A News) (“쓰러지니까 사람들이 몰리는 모습도 있고 그래서 웅성웅성 소리도 났을 거고 그래서 몰랐을 일은 없겠다 생각을 하고. (…) 한동훈 후보 같은 경우도 그런 상황에 대해서 이게 봤지만 제가 생각이 짧았다든지 이런 식으로 바로 인정을 할 건 인정을 했어야지 그걸 뭐 못 봤다, 이렇게 얘기를 하는 거는 정직하지 못한 태도라고 봅니다.” (5월 12일 채널A 뉴스))

The common trait between Yoon Suk-yeol and Han Dong-hoon—both unwilling to admit fault or apologize—is hard to separate from their profession as prosecutors. It’s the result of arrogance from a lifetime of privilege and a habit of treating every issue as a legal conflict. In court, it’s far more advantageous to deny everything consistently than to admit and apologize. The current and former prosecutors who didn’t admit or apologize for illegal acts confirmed in the ‘political prosecution investigation’ are good examples. The root of Yoon Suk-yeol’s descent into martial law, cutting his term short and ending up in prison, also stems from his refusal to admit mistakes. It seems trivial, but it’s a fatal flaw that’s anything but minor. (잘못을 인정하지 않고 사과하기 싫어하는 윤석열·한동훈 두 사람의 공통점은 ‘검사’라는 직업과 분리해서 생각하기 어렵습니다. 평생 특권계급으로 군림해온 오만함, 모든 사안을 법적 갈등으로 간주하는 태도가 몸에 밴 결과입니다. 법정에선 인정하고 사과하는 것보다 모르쇠로 일관하는 쪽이 훨씬 유리하거든요. 이번 ‘정치검찰 국정조사’에서 사실로 확인된 불법 행위조차 인정하거나 사과하지 않았던 전·현직 검사들이 좋은 예입니다. 윤석열이 계엄으로 폭주해 스스로 임기를 단축하고 감옥에 들어간 사태의 출발점도 결국 자신의 잘못을 인정하지 않는 태도에서 비롯했습니다. 사소한 듯하지만, 결코 사소하지 않은 치명적 결함입니다.)

Another worst DNA passed down among prosecutors is ‘lack of empathy.’ This likely stems from their role at a powerful agency with both investigative and prosecutorial powers, accustomed to berating and trapping suspects. Their minds, viewing everyone as potential criminals, have no room for compassion or pity. (검사들에게 유전되는 또 다른 최악의 디엔에이가 ‘공감능력 부족’입니다. 수사권과 기소권을 동시에 가진 권력기관에서 피의자를 닦달하고 옭아매는 역할에 익숙해진 탓일 겁니다. 모든 사람을 잠재적 범죄자로 생각하는 그들의 마음에는 연민이나 동정 따위 생겨날 여유가 없습니다.)

We have experienced countless times under President Yoon Suk-yeol what happens when someone lacking empathy becomes president. You might remember this video: (공감능력이 부족한 사람이 대통령이 되면 어떤 일이 일어나는지 우리는 윤석열 대통령 치하에서 수도 없이 겪었습니다. 여러분, 이 영상 기억하실 겁니다.)

“As I was leaving work, I noticed other apartments down below had already started flooding.” (August 9, 2022, KTV) (“제가 퇴근하면서 보니까 벌써 다른 아파트들이, 아래쪽에 있는 아파트들은 벌써 침수가 시작되더라고요.” (2022년 8월 9일 KTV))

While the capital region’s heavy rain had already begun and apartments were flooding, the president left work as usual, nonchalantly. A family of three died in a semi-basement home in Seoul’s Sillim-dong, and the next day, he visited the house, looking in like at a zoo, saying this. Even with the Itaewon disaster and the death of Marine Chae, he was far from genuinely empathizing with the pain, instead scrambling to downplay and cover up. Yoon has proven with his own actions that empathy is an essential virtue for politicians. (수도권 집중호우가 이미 시작돼서 아파트가 침수되는 걸 보면서도 대통령이라는 사람이 평소처럼 아무렇지 않게 퇴근했습니다. 서울 신림동 반지하 집에서 일가족 3명이 사망했는데, 다음날 이 집을 찾아 동물원 들여다보듯 쳐다보면서 이 얘길 한 겁니다. 이태원 참사와 채상병 사망 사건에 대해서도 진심으로 아픔에 공감하기는커녕, 사건을 축소하고 은폐하는 데 급급했습니다. 공감능력이야말로 정치인이 갖춰야 할 필수 덕목이라는 사실을 윤 전 대통령이 몸 바쳐 증명했습니다.)

Candidate Han Dong-hoon also appears lacking in empathy based on his usual words and actions. He seems aware that this is a major shortcoming for a politician. His insistence that he didn’t notice the reporter’s fall likely stems from fear of revealing this flaw. If you lack empathy, you need to at least fake it, but that’s hard to do in sudden situations. (한동훈 후보 역시 평소 언행으로 보아 공감능력이 부족해 보입니다. 정치인으로선 중대한 단점이라는 사실을 본인도 아는 것 같습니다. 이번 기자 추락 사태를 한사코 인지하지 못했다고 우기는 이유도 공감능력이 부족하다는 자신의 단점이 드러날까 두렵기 때문일 겁니다. 공감능력이 없으면 있는 척이라도 해야 하는데 갑작스러운 상황에서는 잘 될 리가 없죠.)

Candidate Han tries to compensate for this flaw with ‘image-making’ tactics. You might also remember this scene: (한 후보는 이런 자신의 단점을 ‘이미지 메이킹’ 수법으로 보완하려 애를 씁니다. 여러분 이 장면도 기억하실 겁니다.)

Two years ago, as People Power Party leader, he visited a hotel fire scene in Bucheon, Gyeonggi. He glanced at the camera and then awkwardly leaned his chin on his hand. He tried to portray empathy and contemplation over the fire’s tragedy. But when you force it, it shows. He brought on his own ‘bad acting controversy.’ (2년 전 국민의힘 대표 시절 경기 부천 호텔 화재 현장을 찾았을 때인데요. 카메라를 흘깃 쳐다본 뒤 어색하게 턱을 괴는 자세를 취합니다. 화재 현장의 아픔에 공감하며 고뇌하는 장면을 연출하려 한 건데요. 마음에 없는 일을 하면 이렇게 티가 납니다. 스스로 ‘발연기 논란’을 자초했습니다.)

Recently, he posted a video of himself eating rice given by an elderly woman selling vegetables on the street. He aimed for a down-to-earth, approachable image. He probably wanted to shed the aristocratic image from Seoul’s Gangnam. How did you see it? I found the intention too obvious and shallow. (최근엔 길에서 야채를 파는 할머니가 준 밥을 길바닥에서 먹는 영상을 올렸는데요. 서민적이고 털털한 이미지를 연출한 겁니다. 서울 강남 출신의 귀족 이미지를 벗어나고 싶었겠죠. 여러분은 어떻게 보셨습니까? 저는 연출 의도가 너무 뻔해서 얄팍하다고 느꼈습니다.)

I still vividly recall when the media vied to boost Yoon Suk-yeol when he first entered politics. They portrayed him as a common man walking a dog or eating soup at a restaurant. They even cheered his ‘tiger is coming’ image. But the scene that most starkly revealed the real Yoon Suk-yeol was the photo of him putting his leather-shoed feet on a KTX seat. It showed he’s an arrogant person with no concept of public decency or consideration. We shouldn’t be fooled by whitewashed images. (윤석열이 정치판에 처음 등장할 때 언론들이 윤석열을 앞다퉈 띄웠던 장면이 지금도 눈에 선합니다. 개를 끌고 산책을 다니거나 식당에서 국밥을 먹는 서민적 분위기를 연출했죠. ‘범 내려온다’고 고무찬양을 하기도 했고요. 하지만 인간 윤석열을 가장 적나라하게 보여준 장면은 케이티엑스 좌석에 구둣발을 올린 사진이었습니다. 공중도덕이 뭔지, 민폐가 뭔지, 개념 자체가 없는 안하무인의 인간이라는 사실입니다. 분칠된 이미지에 속지 말아야 합니다.)

Most prosecutors are goal-oriented people. Their goals—success or advancement—are clear. The more prominent a prosecutor is within the prosecution, the stronger their obsession with success. That’s why some prosecutors fabricate evidence to achieve results. They are inherently self-centered and inevitably lack empathy. (대개의 검사는 목표 지향형 인간들입니다. 성공 또는 출세라는 목표가 명확한 사람들이죠. 검찰 안에서도 두각을 나타낸 검사일수록 성공에 대한 집착이 더 강할 수밖에 없습니다. 성과를 내기 위해 증거까지 조작하는 검사가 존재하는 이유입니다. 자기 중심성이 강할 수밖에 없고, 공감능력은 부족할 수밖에 없습니다.)

In court, the ‘prosecutor gene’ might be advantageous, but in politics, it becomes poison. One of Korean politics’ most chronic ills is the ‘judicialization of politics,’ where everything is resolved through law. The point when dialogue and compromise began to disappear roughly coincides with the influx of ex-prosecutors in Yeouido. (법정에선 ‘검사 유전자’가 유리할지 모르겠지만, 정치에 쓰이면 독이 됩니다. 한국 정치의 가장 고질적인 병폐가 모든 사안을 법으로 해결하려는 ‘정치의 사법화’인데, 대화와 타협이 사라지기 시작한 시점과 여의도에 검사 출신들이 많아진 시점이 대체로 일치합니다.)

Yoon Suk-yeol, who mobilized the prosecution to eliminate political rivals, represents the peak of this. Candidate Han Dong-hoon, as Minister of Justice under Yoon, stood at the forefront. His ‘fighting cock’ image emerged then too. Can ‘Politician Han Dong-hoon’ cut off the label of being a byproduct and surplus of ‘Yoon Suk-yeol politics’? Can he shed the ‘prosecutor gene’? I’m skeptical. (검찰을 동원해 정적 제거에 나섰던 윤석열이 그 정점에 해당합니다. 한동훈 후보는 윤석열 정부 법무부 장관으로 대열의 선봉에 섰죠. ‘싸움닭’ 이미지도 그때 생겼습니다. ‘정치인 한동훈’은 ‘윤석열 정치’의 부산물이자 잉여물이라는 꼬리표를 스스로 잘라낼 수 있을까요? ‘검사 유전자’를 버릴 수 있을까요? 저는 회의적입니다.)

Candidate Han has touted his opposition to the December 3 emergency martial law as a major achievement and a distinction from Yoon Suk-yeol. But I think even his ‘opposition to martial law’ was a transformation to secure his own political position. (한동훈 후보는 12·3 비상계엄 반대를 자신의 주요한 치적이자 윤석열과의 차별점으로 선전해 왔습니다. 하지만 ‘계엄 반대’마저 한동훈 개인의 정치적 입지 확보를 위한 변신이라고 저는 생각합니다.)

In reality, after the martial law, then-People Power Party leader Han showed erratic behavior, declaring joint governance with then-Prime Minister Han Duck-soo. In the first National Assembly vote on Yoon’s impeachment, Han’s party line was “oppose impeachment.” Yet after Yoon’s impeachment went through, he took all the credit. (실제로 계엄 이후 한동훈 당시 국민의힘 대표는 한덕수 당시 총리와 국정을 공동 운영하겠다고 발표하는 등 오락가락 행보를 보였습니다. 국회의 윤석열 탄핵 1차 표결 때 한 대표가 이끄는 국민의힘 당론은 “탄핵 반대”였습니다. 이랬던 사람이 윤석열 탄핵이 이뤄진 뒤에는 모든 공을 자신에게 돌렸습니다.)

He also displayed despicable behavior, criticizing then-Democratic Party leader Lee Jae-myung, who climbed the National Assembly fence on martial law day and waited in the woods to avoid martial law forces, by saying, “He hid in the woods out of fear.” Despite most people knowing that Lee Jae-myung was the first to rush to the Assembly that day and appeal to citizens via YouTube livestream to “gather at the Assembly,” Han spews such blatant lies. (그러면서 계엄 당일 국회 담장을 넘은 이재명 당시 민주당 대표가 계엄군을 피해 숲에서 대기했던 것을 “무서워서 숲에 숨었다”고 비난하는 비열한 행태를 보였습니다. 계엄 당일 가장 먼저 국회로 달려가면서 유튜브 생방송을 통해 ‘국회로 모여달라’고 시민에게 호소했던 사람이 이재명이었다는 사실을 대다수 국민이 알고 있는데도 이렇게 뻔한 거짓말을 늘어놓습니다.)

Recently, Candidate Han appointed Jeong Hyeong-geun, a former public security prosecutor and Grand National Party lawmaker, as his campaign treasurer. Who is Jeong Hyeong-geun? He is a key figure suspected of directly participating in or ordering numerous torture cases as the head of the National Security Agency’s anti-communism bureau under the notoriously brutal Chun Doo-hwan regime. Revelations by Seo Gyeong-won and Sim Jin-gu about the 1989 North Korea visit case and the 1986 National Liberation Workers’ Party case have continued. When asked about appointing such a person, Candidate Han replied: (최근 한 후보는 공안검사 출신의 정형근 전 한나라당 의원을 후원회장에 임명했죠. 정형근이 누구입니까? 고문으로 악명 높았던 전두환 정권의 안기부 대공수사국장으로서 숱한 고문 사건에 직접 가담했거나 지시했다는 의혹의 당사자입니다. 1989년 서경원 전 의원 방북 사건, 1986년 민족해방노동자당 사건 심진구씨 등의 폭로가 이어졌습니다. 이런 사람을 후원회장에 임명해 놓고 이에 대한 입장을 묻자 한 후보는 이렇게 답합니다.)

“This is a local election, and the candidate is me.” (May 8, MBC ‘Siseon Jipjung’) (“이건 지역 선거고 후보는 저다.” (5월 8일 MBC ‘시선집중’))

Again, a Han Dong-hoon-style diversion. He doesn’t answer the question but shifts the focus. (역시 한동훈식 논점이탈입니다. 묻는 말에 답하지 않고 논점을 이동시킵니다.)

During his campaign, Han often says, “I will do a good job.” What exactly does he mean he’ll do well? Han’s ‘I’ll do well’ politics is as hollow as Yoon Suk-yeol’s ‘uppercut politics.’ It’s less substantive than Ahn Cheol-soo’s ‘new politics’ and more vague than Park Geun-hye’s ‘creative economy.’ There’s no future vision at all. But some things are clear: he’ll fight more fiercely, lie more, and shift blame. Isn’t it time to move beyond the politics of prosecutors? (한 후보는 선거운동을 하면서 “잘 하겠습니다”라는 말을 달고 삽니다. 대체 뭘 잘하겠다는 걸까요? 한동훈의 ‘잘 하겠다’ 정치는 윤석열의 ‘어퍼컷 정치’ 만큼이나 공허합니다. 안철수의 ‘새 정치’보다 내용이 없고, 박근혜의 ‘창조경제’보다 모호합니다. 미래 비전은 전혀 보이지 않습니다. 분명해 보이는 것도 있습니다. 더 사납게 싸우고, 거짓말하고, 책임을 떠넘길 것 같습니다. 이제 그만 검사들의 정치에서 벗어나야 할 때가 되지 않았습니까?)

This has been Nonsseol. (지금까지 논썰이었습니다.)

item.title: June 3 Local Elections: 510 Candidates Win Uncontested…Average Competition Ratio of 1.8 to 1, Lowest Ever (6·3 지방선거, 510명 무투표 당선…평균 경쟁률 1.8대 1 역대 최저)
item.description:
The National Election Commission announced on the 16th that as a result of candidate registration for the June 3 local elections, 513 candidates nationwide have been elected uncontested. There are 307 districts where no vote is needed due to single candidacies or insufficient seats. (6·3 지방선거 후보 등록 결과 전국 후보자 513명이 무투표로 당선됐다고 중앙선거관리위원회가 16일 밝혔다. 단독출마·정수 미달 등으로 인한 무투표 선거구는 307곳이다.)

By election unit, the heads of basic local governments elected uncontested include Kwon Yi-kang, head of Gwangju Seo-gu, Kim Byung-nae, head of Gwangju Nam-gu, and Lim Byung-taek, candidate for mayor of Siheung, Gyeonggi Province, all from the Democratic Party of Korea. Gwangju's Nam-gu and Seo-gu are strongholds for the Democratic Party. In the case of Siheung, although it is located in the metropolitan area, a key battleground in local elections, the main opposition party, People Power Party, failed to field a candidate in this election due to recruitment difficulties. Among regional council members, 108 were elected without a vote in districts including Seoul's Eunpyeong 2nd constituency and Gwanak 1st constituency, while 305 basic council members were confirmed in districts like Seoul's Jongno Na and Ra constituencies. Additionally, 97 proportional representation basic council members, including those in Seoul's Seongbuk and Dobong districts, were also elected uncontested, totaling 510 local council members. (선거 단위별로는 무투표 당선이 결정된 기초단체장 후보는 김이강 광주 서구청장, 김병내 광주 남구청장, 임병택 경기 시흥시장 후보 3명으로 모두 더불어민주당 소속이다. 광주 남·서구는 민주당 강세 지역이다. 시흥시의 경우 지방선거 승부처인 수도권에 자리 잡고 있으나 제1야당인 국민의힘은 구인난으로 이번 선거에서 후보자를 내지 못했다. 광역의원은 서울 은평 2선거구·관악 1선거구 등에서 108명, 기초의원은 서울 종로 나선거구·라선거구 등에서 305명, 비례 기초의원은 서울 성북·도봉을 비롯해 97명 등 지방의원 510명도 투표 없이 당선이 확정됐다.)

Meanwhile, a total of 7,829 candidates registered for this June 3 local elections and National Assembly by-elections. The average competition ratio was 1.8 to 1, matching the level of the 2022 local elections, which had the lowest ratio ever. (한편, 이번 6·3 지방선거와 국회의원 재보궐선거에는 모두 7829명이 후보로 등록했다. 평균 경쟁률은 1.8대 1로 역대 최저치였던 지난 2022년 지방선거와 같은 수준을 보였다.)

In this election, 16 heads of higher-level local governments, 227 heads of basic local governments, 933 regional council members (including proportional representation), 3,035 basic council members (including proportional representation), 16 superintendents of education, and 14 National Assembly members will be elected. In the elections for heads of higher-level local governments, 54 candidates registered, resulting in a competition ratio of 3.4 to 1. (이번 선거에서는 광역단체장 16명, 기초단체장 227명, 광역의원(비례 포함) 933명, 기초의원(비례 포함) 3035명, 교육감 16명, 국회의원 14명을 선출한다. 광역단체장 선거는 후보 54명이 등록해 3.4 대 1의 경쟁률을 기록했다.)

For heads of basic local governments, 585 candidates (2.6 to 1 ratio), regional council members 1,657 (2.1 to 1), and basic council members 4,402 (1.7 to 1) have thrown their hats into the ring. Proportional representation regional council members see 354 candidates (2.7 to 1), proportional representation basic council members 672 (1.7 to 1), and superintendents of education 58 (3.6 to 1) running. In the National Assembly by-elections, 47 candidates are running, with a competition ratio of 3.4 to 1. (기초단체장 선거는 585명(2.6대 1), 광역의원 1657명(2.1대 1), 기초의원 4402명(1.7대 1)의 후보가 출사표를 냈다. 비례 광역의원은 354명(2.7대 1), 비례 기초의원은 672명(1.7대 1), 교육감 58명(3.6대 1)이 후보로 나선다. 국회의원 재보선의 경우 47명이 출마해 3.4대 1의 경쟁률을 보였다.)

Park Ji-young, Reporter jyp@hani.co.kr (박지영 기자 jyp@hani.co.kr)

item.title: Only Photojournalists Know Jung Cheong-rae and Jang Dong-hyuk's 'Habits' [Oops Gura] (사진기자만 아는 정청래와 장동혁의 ‘버릇’ [웁스구라])
item.description:
After covering the National Assembly and daily observing lawmakers through the camera viewfinder, I’ve come to notice unique habits and traits of politicians that only photojournalists can pick up on. (국회를 출입하며 카메라 뷰파인더로 국회의원들을 매일 보다 보니 사진기자만이 느끼는 정치인들의 독특한 버릇과 특징이 보인다.)

First, Jung Cheong-rae, the leader of the Democratic Party of Korea, has an undeniable left-wing (?) instinct. During meetings, when speaking while reading from a script, he lifts his head and only looks to the left. For newspaper production, it’s essential to capture moments where the speaker’s gaze shifts left, right, and center, but this drives me crazy. However, there’s a twist. When he speaks off-script—essentially ad-libbing—he only looks to the right. So, if he suddenly deviates from his script during a speech, I silently anticipate, ‘Ah, now he’ll look to the right,’ and focus my shutter energy. <<> Conversely, Jang Dong-hyuk, the leader of the People Power Party, has a primal right-wing instinct. When he occasionally lifts his head during meeting speeches, he only looks to the right. Unlike Jung, even when ad-libbing, he rarely looks left—to the point where I wonder, ‘Does he really dislike leftists that much?’ Jang also has a peculiar routine: after finishing his speech, he turns off the microphone switch with one hand while gripping the mic stand with the other and bending it downward. Then, he aligns the script he was reading with a certain imaginary baseline—like the edge of the table or the tip of the mic—and adjusts its angle. It seems almost compulsive. <<> Han Dong-hoon, the former leader of the People Power Party, has frequently appeared in gossip articles since his appointment as Yoon Suk Yeol’s first Minister of Justice, through his tenure as party leader, and even now, thanks to his distinctive fashion sense—from glasses to clothes and shoes. Among these, his black horn-rimmed glasses have become iconic. However, the thick frames occasionally cover his eyes and cast shadows on his face. Particularly from side angles when he’s speaking, it’s hard to capture his eyes. Photos in newspapers without visible pupils rarely get used since facial expressions are lost. Perhaps due to the weight, he often pushes up his glasses with his fingers—a gesture typically used in contexts of distress or confusion. Han’s horn-rimmed glasses, like political symbols, don’t always convey a purely positive image. <<> Sometimes, politicians’ habits can appear positive to photojournalists. Song Eon-seok, the floor leader of the People Power Party, always extends both hands when shaking hands. As the opposition’s floor leader, who must frequently negotiate and confront the ruling party, Song—at least during handshakes—doesn’t come across as confrontational or hostile. <<> Additionally, Park Chan-dae, former floor leader of the Democratic Party of Korea, speaks clearly with his head lifted high, eyes wide open, and mouth wide. He’s so photogenic that photojournalists joke, ‘We wish he’d just stay as floor leader forever.’ If there were an award photojournalists could give politicians, he’d likely be a strong candidate for a ‘Photogenic’ prize. <<> On the flip side, the worst for photojournalists is a politician who never lifts their head during a speech and just reads from a script. Capturing a shot where they have their eyes open and head raised feels like a gamble, making the coverage incredibly taxing. Unable to shift positions because you don’t know when they’ll look up, you have to stay locked in the viewfinder, focused on when the speaker will raise their head. From the morning, when party schedules like supreme council meetings pile up, it drains all your energy. I find myself silently wishing that seat would be filled by someone else soon. <<> Personally, I do have political parties and politicians I support, but the moment I pick up the camera and press the shutter, it barely matters. When I’m stuck photographing a politician who won’t cooperate, I find myself muttering complaints under my breath. Why would I bother about political lines when it’s making me physically exhausted? After all, in politics, the best person is the one who makes my body comfortable. Ah, don’t misunderstand—that’s only in that moment. <<> Yoon Woon-sik, Senior Reporter yws@hani.co.kr (우선 정청래 더불어민주당 대표는 숨길 수 없는 좌파(?)본능을 가지고 있다. 각종 회의에서 원고를 보면서 발언할 때 정 대표는 고개를 들어 왼쪽만 본다. 신문제작을 위해서는 좌·우 그리고 가운데에 시선을 두고 말하는 장면이 기본적으로 있어야하는데 속이 터진다. 그런데 반전이 있다. 원고에 없는 내용을 말할 때, 이른바 애드립을 칠 때는 또 오른쪽만 본다. 그래서 정 대표가 발언하다 갑자기 원고에 없는 얘기를 할 땐 ‘아, 이젠 오른쪽을 보겠구나’라고 속으로 기대를 하면서 셔터에 기를 모은다.)

item.title: "Encouraging Blind Voting, or Mystique?"… People Power Party Criticizes Democratic Party for 'Minimizing Debates' (“깜깜이 투표 조장, 신비주의인가?”…국힘, ‘토론 최소화’ 민주당 비판)
item.description:
The People Power Party has criticized the Democratic Party of Korea's policy of 'minimizing debates' by its candidates in major battlegrounds for the June 3 local elections, accusing them of "playing a bed football election." (국민의힘이 6·3 지방선거 주요 격전지에 나선 더불어민주당 후보들의 ‘토론 최소화’ 방침을 두고 “침대 축구로 선거를 치르고 있다”며 비판했다.)

People Power Party leader Jang Dong-hyuk posted on his Facebook on the 16th, saying, "Democratic Party candidates have all laid down. They refuse to debate and have launched into bed football," adding, "The end result will be a come-from-behind theater goal." He claimed, "Candidate Jung Won-oh (for Seoul mayor) has more than a few things to hide, candidate Choo Mi-ae (for Gyeonggi governor) knows nothing about Gyeonggi Province's affairs, and candidate Park Chan-dae (for Incheon mayor) is afraid of debates because Lee Jae-myung's crimes might be exposed again." (장동혁 국민의힘 대표는 16일 자신의 페이스북에 글을 올려 “민주당 후보들은 다 드러누웠다. 토론도 거부하고 침대 축구에 돌입했다”며 “그 끝은 역전 극장 골”이라고 말했다. 그는 “정원오 (서울시장) 후보는 걸리는 게 한두 개가 아니고, 추미애 (경기지사) 후보는 경기도 사정을 아는 게 없고, 박찬대 (인천시장) 후보는 이재명 범죄가 또 드러날까 싶어서 토론이 무서운 것”이라고 주장했다.)

It has been reported that Democratic Party candidates, including Seoul mayoral candidate Jung Won-oh, Gyeonggi governor candidate Choo Mi-ae, and Busan North Gap by-election candidate Ha Jung-woo, plan to participate in only one debate before the election. This means they will only fulfill the statutory debate obligation stipulated by the Public Official Election Act, which requires "at least one debate." In past local elections, two to five debates were typically held. (정원오 서울시장 후보를 비롯해 추미애 경기지사 후보, 하정우 부산 북갑 국회의원 보궐선거 후보 등 민주당 후보들은 선거 전 한 차례 토론회에만 참여할 계획인 것으로 알려졌다. 공직선거법에서 ‘1회 이상’이라고 규정하는 법정 토론 의무만 지키겠다는 것이다. 역대 지방선거에선 2~5차례 토론이 이뤄졌었다.)

People Power Party senior spokesperson Park Seong-hoon also issued a commentary on the same day, criticizing, "Democratic Party candidates are fundamentally blocking the public's right to know with their petty avoidance of debates and bed football tactics, blatantly encouraging 'blind voting' among voters." He further criticized, "What's even more outrageous is that candidates who avoid debates watched by the entire nation are frequently appearing on broadcasts by hardcore pro-Democratic Party YouTubers," adding, "It's truly a sight too unbearable to behold." Park also noted that the only debate schedule Jung accepted is "at 11 PM on the 28th, just 7 hours before early voting begins," calling it "a despicable trick to force voters into blind voting, essentially telling them to 'vote without asking or questioning anything.'" (박성훈 국민의힘 수석대변인도 이날 논평을 내고 “민주당 후보들이 치졸한 토론 기피 침대 축구로 국민의 알 권리를 원천 차단하고 유권자들에게 ‘깜깜이 투표’를 노골적으로 조장하고 있다”고 비판했다. 이어 “더 기가 막힌 건 전 국민이 지켜보는 토론을 기피하는 후보들이 강성 친민주당 성향 유튜버들의 방송에는 문턱이 닳도록 드나들고 있는 행태”라며 “참으로 목불인견”이라고 비판했다. 이어 박 대변인은 정 후보가 수용한 유일한 토론회 일정이 “사전투표 시작을 고작 7시간 앞둔 28일 밤 11시”라며 “사실상 유권자에게 ‘아무것도 묻지도 따지지도 말고 찍으라’는 깜깜이 투표를 강요하는 비열한 꼼수”라고 했다.)

Independent candidate Han Dong-hoon, who is running in the Busan North Gap by-election, also criticized via Facebook, saying, "I don't understand why political newcomer Ha Jung-woo is employing a mystique strategy. Is he Seo Taiji or something?" (부산 북갑 보선에 출마한 한동훈 무소속 후보도 페이스북을 통해 “정치 신인인 하정우 후보가 그가 어째서 신비주의 전략을 구사하는지 모르겠다. 본인이 서태지인가”라고 비판했다.)

Reporter Park Ji-young jyp@hani.co.kr (박지영 기자 jyp@hani.co.kr)

item.title: [Jung Wook-sik Column] The Korean Peninsula Peace: Time to Seek Harmony Between Power and Institutions ([정욱식 칼럼] 한반도 평화, 힘과 제도의 조화를 모색할 때)
item.description:
Witnessing the wars erupting across the globe recently, one truly realizes the saying, 'Ending a war is far harder than starting one.' The Russia-Ukraine war, which began with Russia's illegal invasion in February 2022, has yet to even approach the threshold of an end. Amidst this, U.S. President Donald Trump, who took office, boasted he would end the Russia-Ukraine war "within 24 hours," but along with Israel, he has started another war against Iran. Israel's wars against Palestine and Lebanon continue with barbaric use of force, rendering intermittent ceasefire agreements meaningless. <<> What about the Korean Peninsula? The Armistice Agreement signed on July 27, 1953, was deeply 'temporary' in nature, containing a clause to conclude a peace treaty through "high-level political negotiations within three months." However, with nearly 73 years passing without a single substantive peace treaty negotiation, the armistice state—neither war nor peace—has solidified into a system. So, is an official end to the Korean War possible? <<> For starters, the South Korean and U.S. presidents have expressed their will for ending the war and establishing peace on the Korean Peninsula. President Trump stated at the ROK-U.S. summit on October 29, 2025, "I know that the Korean Peninsula is officially in a state of war," adding, "We will look into what we can do to fix all of this." He particularly vowed, "I will work very hard with Kim Jong-un to rectify this." President Lee Jae-myung also pledged in his March 1st Independence Movement Day address in 2026, "I will make every effort to transition the armistice system into a peace system." This was the first time President Lee, since taking office in June 2025, raised the topic of "transitioning the armistice system to a peace system" in a public setting. <<> What about Joseon (North Korea)'s stance? Establishing a peace system through a peace treaty focused on ending the war and preventing war, along with its implementation, had long been a demand of Joseon. However, after 2019, references to a peace treaty or peace system disappeared from Joseon's discourse. Even in 2020, the 70th year since the outbreak of the Korean War, and in 2023, the 70th year since the signing of the Armistice Agreement, there was no mention of it whatsoever. This remains the case even after Presidents Lee Jae-myung and Trump expressed their will for ending the war and a peace system. This allows for an interpretation that Joseon is becoming indifferent to a peace treaty. <<> The shift in stance by China and Russia is also notable. China, once considered a party to peace treaty negotiations alongside the two Koreas and the U.S., had advocated for the 'dual-track approach' of establishing a peace system and denuclearization as a solution to the Korean Peninsula issue. However, after China's State Council mentioned in May 2025 "promoting the construction of a peace system on the Korean Peninsula and the denuclearization process in parallel," expressions indicating the dual-track approach or 'denuclearization' have disappeared from official Chinese government documents and officials' remarks. Russia, which previously aligned with China, has effectively recognized Joseon as a nuclear weapons state following the 2024 June North Korea-Russia summit and the re-establishment of their alliance. <<> The impact of the U.S.-Israel-Iran war also warrants attention. Witnessing the illegal U.S.-Israel invasion of Iran, Joseon is further solidifying its stance on securing war deterrence through nuclear forces and its refusal to denuclearize. Notably, recalling how Iran was exploited twice during negotiations, Joseon will likely consider it best to avoid any entanglement with the U.S. unless the U.S. definitively drops its denuclearization demands. Conversely, it is becoming increasingly difficult for the U.S. to abandon its denuclearization demands. Since the Trump administration has emphasized the core purpose of the war against Iran as 'preventing nuclear weapons possession,' appearing to tolerate Joseon's nuclear armament could trigger a political backlash. If the positions of both sides are not coordinated, Trump's pledge to "meet Kim Jong-un and discuss ending the war" is likely to remain a wishful aspiration. <<> As such, a peace treaty on the Korean Peninsula and the linked denuclearization are sinking into a thick fog. Amidst this, 'peaceful coexistence' is emerging as a new keyword. The Lee Jae-myung government has put forward peaceful coexistence as a core goal of its North Korea policy. Joseon has also recently begun mentioning peaceful coexistence. Chairman Kim Jong-un, after hinting at the possibility of peaceful coexistence specifically directed at the U.S. following the launch of the second Trump administration, stated in his policy speech at the Supreme People's Assembly in late March 2026, "Whether the adversaries choose confrontation or peaceful coexistence is their choice, and we are prepared to respond to any choice." Notably, unlike before, he used the plural form "adversaries," which can be interpreted as remarks targeting South Korea and Japan, not just the U.S. <<> However, the 'peaceful coexistence' that South Korea and Joseon speak of 'with one voice' is closer to 'same bed, different dreams.' The Lee Jae-myung government's theory of peaceful coexistence rests on one pillar of building strong self-reliant defense capabilities, and another pillar of advancing the peace system and denuclearization process. In contrast, Joseon's mentioned peaceful coexistence presupposes its status as a nuclear weapons state. It is in this context that Joseon demands that the U.S. and other "adversaries" drop their denuclearization demands as a core condition for peaceful coexistence. <<> This fundamental difference in positions raises the question: 'In what way can peaceful coexistence be realized?' The most desirable method would be to conclude a peace treaty replacing the Armistice Agreement. However, Joseon has turned its interest away from a peace treaty linked to denuclearization. China and Russia no longer mention the 'dual-track approach' either. This means that as long as South Korea and the U.S. adhere to a linkage between a peace treaty and denuclearization, it is becoming difficult even to open the door for peace treaty negotiations. <<> One alternative to consider is promoting the conclusion of a peace treaty while the ROK-U.S. alliance and Joseon tacitly acknowledge each other's war deterrence capabilities. This involves seeking a harmony between 'peace through power,' where South Korea's self-reliant defense and the U.S. extended deterrence balance Joseon's nuclear deterrence, and 'peace through institutions,' achieved by signing a peace treaty. The former aims to back the vulnerabilities inherent in the latter with power, while the latter aims to manage and control the risks of arms races and security dilemmas inherent in the former through political and military confidence-building. <<> Of course, the likelihood of South Korea and the U.S. tacitly accepting Joseon's nuclear weapons is low. Conversely, the more they insist on denuclearization, the further denuclearization and a peace system drift away. The solution to this dilemma lies in 'creative ambiguity.' This involves including a phrase in the peace treaty with the intent of "jointly striving for a world free of nuclear war and nuclear weapons." <<> Jung Wook-sik, Director of the Hankyoreh Peace Institute and Head of Peace Network, wooksik@gmail.com (최근 지구촌 곳곳에서 벌어지고 있는 전쟁을 보면, ‘전쟁은 시작하는 것보다 끝내는 것이 훨씬 어렵다’는 말을 실감하게 된다. 2022년 2월 러시아의 불법적인 침공으로 시작된 러시아-우크라이나 전쟁은 아직까지도 종전의 문턱에조차 다가서지 못하고 있다. 이 와중에 집권한 미국의 도널드 트럼프 대통령은 러-우 전쟁을 “24시간 내”에 끝내겠다고 호언장담했지만, 이스라엘과 함께 이란을 상대로 또 하나의 전쟁을 시작하고 말았다. 이스라엘의 팔레스타인 및 레바논을 상대로 한 전쟁도 간헐적인 휴전 합의를 무색하게 할 정도로 야만적인 무력사용이 계속되고 있다.)

item.title: Why spend taxes on cheering for a North Korean women’s football team? Let’s clear up the curiosity about the ‘joint cheering squad’ (북 여자축구단 응원에 왜 세금 쓰냐고요? ‘공동응원’ 궁금증 풀어드립니다)
item.description:
At 7 PM on May 20, the semifinal match of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Women’s Champions League (AWCL) will be held at Suwon World Cup Stadium between South Korea’s Suwon FC Women and North Korea’s Naegohyang Women’s Football Team. Amid growing domestic and international interest in this event, over 200 civilian organizations have formed a ‘2026 AFC-AWCL Women’s Football Joint Cheering Squad.’ As the head of the cheering squad, I aim to address key questions. (5월20일 오후 7시 수원종합운동장에선 한국의 수원FC 위민과 조선(북한)의 내고향여자축구단의 아시아축구연맹(AFC) 여자 챔피언스리그(AWCL) 4강전이 열립니다. 이에 대한 국내외의 관심이 고조되고 있는 가운데, 200여개 민간단체들은 ‘2026 AFC-AWCL 여자축구 공동응원단’을 결성했습니다. 응원단 단장으로서 주요 궁금증에 답하고자 합니다.)

—Why spend our citizens’ taxes on cheering for the Naegohyang Women’s Football Team? (―왜 내고향여자축구단 응원에 우리 국민의 세금을 쓰나요?)

“When the Ministry of Unification decided to support the joint cheering with the Inter-Korean Exchange and Cooperation Fund, some media outlets ran reports with headlines like ‘Government provides 300 million won to civilian groups for cheering North Korean football team.’ This has led to criticism labeling it as ‘state-led cheering.’ However, the formation of the joint cheering squad was not a government request but an initiative led by civilian organizations, which then consulted with the government. Additionally, our cheering squad supports the performance of both teams, not just one. Since the primary purpose of the Exchange and Cooperation Fund is to support inter-Korean exchanges and cooperation, there are diverse opinions on whether supporting joint cheering aligns with this goal. We believe this joint cheering does serve that purpose. While mindful of critical views, we will do our utmost to ensure that taxpayer money is not wasted.” (“통일부가 남북교류협력기금으로 공동 응원을 지원하기로 의결하자 일부 언론에선 ‘정부, 북한 축구단 응원 민간단체에 3억원 지원’이라는 취지의 보도를 내보냈습니다. 이로 인해 ‘관제 응원’이라는 비난까지 나오고 있습니다. 하지만 공동응원단 구성은 정부의 요청이 아니라 민간단체들이 먼저 추진하고 정부와 협의하는 과정에서 이뤄진 것입니다. 또 우리 응원단은 특정 팀이 아닌 양 팀 모두의 선전을 응원합니다. 교류협력기금은 남북교류협력을 지원하는 데에 주목적이 있는 만큼, 공동 응원 지원이 이 목적에 부합하느냐에 대해서는 다양한 의견이 있습니다. 저희는 이번 공동응원이 그 목적에 부합한다고 판단합니다. 비판적인 의견에도 유념하면서 국민 세금이 헛되이 쓰이지 않도록 최선을 다하겠습니다.”)

—It’s been reported that the joint cheering squad was unilaterally announced without prior consultation with Suwon FC Women and its supporters? (―공동응원단을 결성하면서 수원FC 위민 구단 및 서포터스와 사전 협의를 하지 않고 일방적으로 발표했다고 하던데요?)

“First, we express our respect for Suwon FC Women and its supporters for their efforts to develop women’s football despite challenging circumstances. The goal of the club and supporters is to win the semifinal and advance to the finals. The purpose of the joint cheering squad is to support the performance of both teams so that the two core values of sports—‘fair play’ and ‘peace’—can be realized on the field. We conveyed to the supporters that our objectives differ, and they expressed understanding.” (“먼저 수원FC위민 구단 및 서포터스가 어려운 여건 속에서도 여자축구의 발전을 위해 노력하고 있는 데에 경의를 표합니다. 구단과 서포터스의 목표는 4강전에서 승리해 결승에 진출하는 것입니다. 공동응원단의 취지는 스포츠의 양대 정신인 ‘페어플레이’와 ‘평화’가 경기장에서 구현될 수 있도록 양 팀 모두의 선전을 응원하는 데에 있습니다. 저희는 목적이 다르다는 점을 서포터스에 전했고 서포터스도 이해를 표했습니다.”)

—Why do you use the term ‘Joseon’ (North Korea) alongside? (―‘조선’(북한)이라고 병기하는 이유는 무엇인가요?)

“Considering this is a club competition, not a national match, we plan not to use national names at the stadium. However, when necessary outside the match, we will use the terms together. This takes into account both the intention to welcome the Naegohyang Women’s Football Team’s visit to South Korea and wish for their success, and the lack of public consensus on using the official national name. As South Korea and North Korea will likely meet in various international sports events in the future, we believe public discussion is needed on how best to refer to them.” (“일단 국가 대항전이 아니라 클럽 대항전인 점을 감안해 경기장에서 국호를 사용하지 않을 계획입니다. 다만 경기 이외에 국호 사용이 필요할 경우 병기하고자 합니다. 이는 내고향여자축구단의 방한을 환영하고 선전을 기원한다는 취지와 공식 국호 사용에 대한 국민적 합의가 아직 부족하다는 점을 두루 고려한 것입니다. 앞으로도 여러 국제스포츠 경기에서 한국과 조선(북한)이 만나게 될 텐데요. 어떻게 호칭하는 것이 바람직한지에 대한 공론화가 필요하다고도 봅니다.”)

—Will this event contribute to improving inter-Korean relations? (―이번 대회가 남북관계 개선에 기여할까요?)

“Given North Korea’s declaration of ‘hostile two states,’ the decision for the Naegohyang team to visit South Korea surprised many. While various interpretations exist, from the perspective of inter-Korean relations, it can be seen as reflecting a reduction in tensions. If the two sides were still exchanging leaflets and trash balloons and blaring propaganda broadcasts like two years ago, this visit would have been difficult. The charm of sports lies in engaging in fierce competition while sharing a spirit of friendship and peace. We hope the players from both sides can fully showcase this charm, and that our citizens and people worldwide, who are deeply interested in this match, can also enjoy it. These moments, accumulated, will bring warmth to inter-Korean relations.” (“조선(북한)이 ‘적대적 두 국가’를 선언한 상황에서 내고향팀의 방한 결정은 많은 이들의 예상을 뛰어넘은 것인데요. 이에 대해서는 다양한 해석이 존재하겠지만, 남북관계 차원에서 보자면 긴장완화가 반영된 것이라고 할 수 있습니다. 2년 전처럼 양측이 전단과 오물을 풍선에 담아 날리고 확성기 방송을 틀고 있었다면, 내고향팀의 방한은 어려웠을 겁니다. 스포츠의 매력은 치열한 승부를 벌이면서도 그 속에서 우애와 평화의 정신을 나누자는 데에 있습니다. 양 팀 선수가 이러한 매력을 마음껏 발산하고 이 경기에 관심이 많은 우리 국민과 세계인들도 이 매력을 만끽할 수 있기를 바랍니다. 이러한 모습이 쌓이면 남북관계에도 온기가 전해질 것입니다.”)

—Do you plan to continue cheering in the future? (―앞으로도 계속 응원할 계획인가요?)

“While further discussions with other organizations are needed, the Hankyoreh Unification Culture Foundation and Peace Network will continue to support athletes from South Korea and North Korea. This autumn, the Asian Games will be held in Japan, and next year, both South Korea and North Korea have qualified for the Brazil Women’s World Cup. Additionally, in 2028, the Pyongyang Asian Table Tennis Championships and the Los Angeles Olympics are scheduled. We plan to recruit citizen cheering squads to actively support at these events alongside overseas compatriots. We hope many people will join us on this journey.” (“다른 단체들과는 후속 논의가 필요하겠지만, 한겨레통일문화재단과 평화네트워크는 우리나라와 조선(북한) 선수를 계속 응원할 것입니다. 올해 가을에는 일본에서 아시안게임이 있고, 내년 브라질 여자월드컵 대회에는 한국과 조선(북한)이 동반 진출한 상황입니다. 또 2028년에는 평양 아시아탁구대회와 미국 LA 올림픽이 예정되어 있습니다. 저희는 시민 응원단을 모집해 해외 동포들과 함께 이들 대회에서 열심히 응원하고자 합니다. 이 여정에 많은 사람들이 함께 할 수 있기를 바랍니다.”)

Jung Wook-sik, Director of the Hankyoreh Peace Institute and Representative of Peace Network wooksik@gmail.com (정욱식 한겨레평화연구소장 겸 평화네트워크 대표 wooksik@gmail.com )

item.title: Busan Buk-gu: Yoon Suk Yeol and Han Dong-hoon’s Bloody Infighting… What Will Be the Outcome? (부산북갑, 윤석열과 한동훈의 골육상쟁…그 결말은?)
item.description:
The heat surrounding the National Assembly by-elections, held alongside the June 3 nationwide local elections, is rivaling that of the local elections themselves. Among them, the most attention is focused on Busan's Buk-gu district. <<> Competing are Ha Jung-woo of the Democratic Party of Korea, who was drafted after serving as a senior presidential secretary for AI future planning; Park Min-shik of the People Power Party, a former minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs under the Yoon Suk Yeol administration; and Han Dong-hoon, an independent candidate who once led the People Power Party but was expelled by its current leader, Jang Dong-hyuk. <<> Busan Buk-gu carries political significance and repercussions far beyond a single parliamentary seat. This is because the contest is between Park Min-shik and Han Dong-hoon, or more precisely, between Jang Dong-hyuk and Han Dong-hoon, and between Yoon Suk Yeol and Han Dong-hoon. <<> Recent opinion polls show support in the order of Ha Jung-woo, Han Dong-hoon, and Park Min-shik. Adding the support rates of Han Dong-hoon and Park Min-shik simply gives a figure higher than Ha Jung-woo's. However, in hypothetical head-to-head matchups between Ha Jung-woo and Han Dong-hoon, and Ha Jung-woo and Park Min-shik, Ha Jung-woo emerges victorious. Strange, isn’t it? Why is that? <<> There are two reasons. First, the fragmentation of the People Power Party’s support base. A significant number of Han Dong-hoon supporters have no intention of voting for Park Min-shik, even if it means Ha Jung-woo wins. Similarly, many of Park Min-shik’s supporters refuse to vote for Han Dong-hoon, even if it leads to a Ha Jung-woo victory. <<> Second, the ‘strategic choice’ of opinion poll respondents. Respondents in hypothetical matchups are well aware of how their answers might influence candidate unification. <<> Supporters of Han Dong-hoon might either choose not to respond or even state they would support Ha Jung-woo in a hypothetical Ha-Park matchup. This is to engineer unification in favor of Han Dong-hoon through poll responses. Park Min-shik’s supporters likely act similarly. However, when it comes to actually voting after unification, they may make different choices. <<> The contest between Park Min-shik and Han Dong-hoon is a kind of bloody infighting—a conflict between bone and flesh. Hatred towards someone who was once on the same side but later split off is often far more intense than hatred towards someone who was always an opponent. <<> Han Dong-hoon was once a core member of the ‘Yoon Suk Yeol faction’ during his time as a prosecutor. President Yoon Suk Yeol appointed him as Minister of Justice and later, ahead of the general election, as emergency committee chairperson of the People Power Party. The two were one entity. They were soulmates. <<> However, the conflict surrounding First Lady Kim Keon Hee intensified, leading to their split. After the crushing defeat in the general election, Han Dong-hoon stepped down as emergency committee chairperson, but despite opposition from President Yoon, he was elected party leader at the July 23 national convention with 62.84% of the vote (80% from party members, 20% from a general public opinion poll). Party members held President Yoon responsible for the general election defeat and gave Han Dong-hoon another chance. <<> The fates of the two men diverged completely on the night of December 3, 2024. Immediately after President Yoon Suk Yeol declared martial law, Han Dong-hoon, as party leader, issued a statement to the press through the party’s public relations office. <<> “The President’s declaration of martial law is wrong. We will join the people to stop it. Han Dong-hoon, Leader of the People Power Party.” <<> Short but powerful. It was an immense display of quick thinking. That night, upon seeing Han Dong-hoon’s message, I too judged that President Yoon’s martial law could not succeed. <<> In truth, Han Dong-hoon should never have entered politics in the first place. He had been a prosecutor his entire life. Like President Yoon, he is someone who doesn't understand politics—a ‘political ignoramus’. <<> During his time as emergency committee chairperson, President Yoon directly asked Han Dong-hoon not to run for office, whether in a local constituency or as a proportional representative. The reason was that this was necessary to win the general election. <<> Han Dong-hoon agreed. He reasoned that “Yeouido is a space where people with long political careers and cunning experience gather, a space of clashing ambitions, and to stand before them, I needed a catalyst to establish my leadership.” It is surprising that he viewed the position of National Assembly member, a representative of the people, as a potential sacrifice—a mere tool to build political leadership. <<> Han Dong-hoon also has serious issues with the empathy and attitude required of a politician. Yet, his judgment and actions on the night of December 3 were highly appropriate and correct. <<> Former leader Han Dong-hoon was expelled from the People Power Party by current leader Jang Dong-hyuk. The person most opposed to the unification of Han Dong-hoon and Park Min-shik is also Jang Dong-hyuk. Why is that? Because he became leader by riding the ‘Yoon Again’ wave. Because he is an avatar of Yoon Suk Yeol. On the afternoon of May 15, Jang Dong-hyuk posted this on Facebook: <<> “The People Power Party must win in this local election. We are the last breakwater protecting South Korea’s liberal democracy and the people’s livelihood. But victory cannot be an end in itself. Unification based solely on vote counting doesn’t align with conservative values. It cannot be the path to unity or victory. Candidates who received the party’s nomination through the choice of party members must remember this. The issue of unification must also follow the will of party members and the party.” <<> If not victory, what is the goal? The goal is likely ‘Yoon Again’. The goal is likely to finish off Han Dong-hoon, the symbolic figure of ‘anti-Yoon Suk Yeol’. <<> A political party is a group of people who share values. But only by governing can those values be realized. Therefore, the purpose of a party is to govern. It is to win elections. Jang Dong-hyuk seems unaware of the fundamentals of politics. <<> Most People Power Party lawmakers from Busan districts are calling for the unification of Park Min-shik and Han Dong-hoon. Busan mayoral candidate Park Hyung-joon also demands unification. If they unify, it could create a favorable trend for the People Power Party not just in Busan but nationwide in this election. However, the unification of Park Min-shik and Han Dong-hoon is difficult. There are two reasons. <<> First, candidate unification itself is inherently difficult. Unification requires a justification. The goal must be clear. A minimum level of human respect between candidates is also necessary. Park Min-shik and Han Dong-hoon have vastly differing views. They seem to hate each other more than they hate Ha Jung-woo. <<> Second, the division among party members and supporters. Jang Dong-hyuk’s statement that “unification must follow the will of party members and the party” is correct. However, party members and supporters are split. They have been sharply divided into two camps since the moment President Yoon declared martial law on December 3. Comments on Han Dong-hoon’s anti-martial law Facebook post included: <<> “By your swift response, you have saved conservatism once again. The people owe you a great debt. I will protect you, leader, to the end.” <<> “Why did you go to the National Assembly when you are not a member? Doing nothing until such an emergency occurred, are you there out of ambition to become president?” <<> Han Dong-hoon follows the People Power Party supporters who opposed the martial law. Jang Dong-hyuk follows the supporters who endorsed the martial law. Unification cannot be achieved through their personal decisions alone. <<> Attention is now focused on the post-election period. Realistically, there are roughly three possible scenarios. <<> First, what if Ha Jung-woo wins, Han Dong-hoon comes second, and Park Min-shik comes third, as polls indicate? Jang Dong-hyuk would face a significant blow. He would rapidly lose his leadership within the People Power Party. <<> Second, what if Ha Jung-woo wins, Park Min-shik comes second, and Han Dong-hoon comes third? Han Dong-hoon would suffer a major setback. A comeback might become difficult. Conversely, Jang Dong-hyuk would likely hold his ground, insisting he was right. <<> Third, what if Han Dong-hoon wins? Regardless of the local election results, Jang Dong-hyuk’s leadership could collapse. The People Power Party could fall into even deeper internal strife than now, or even split entirely into the ‘Yoon Again’ faction and the ‘Pro-Han Dong-hoon’ faction. ‘Representative Han Dong-hoon’ would emerge as the standard-bearer for conservative reconstruction. <<> Park Ji-won, a seasoned Democratic Party lawmaker who has been through many political battles, recently said, “If Cho Kuk in Pyeongtaek-eul, Han Dong-hoon in Busan Buk-gu, and Kim Kwan-young in Jeonbuk win, the Democratic Party will be in real trouble.” This was a statement expressing concern about Ha Jung-woo’s potential defeat in Busan Buk-gu. <<> However, if Han Dong-hoon wins, the People Power Party would have an opportunity to shed the ‘Yoon Again’ faction and evolve into a rational, reformist conservative party. In the long run, such a change in the People Power Party would also benefit the Democratic Party. On May 15, at a central election committee meeting in Jeju, Representative Jung Cheong-rae said: <<> “A strong opposition forces the ruling party to be on edge and become stronger. I do not want the People Power Party under Jang Dong-hyuk to collapse. I hope it normalizes. I hope it comes to its senses. I hope we can have fair competition. Some people call Jang Dong-hyuk a strategic asset or something, but I’m not entirely happy to agree with that. I simply hope the People Power Party can be reborn as a healthy, common-sense party that the South Korean people can relate to. The Democratic Party wants to compete fairly on vision and policy, and settle the outcome based on character and capability.” <<> I believe Representative Jung Cheong-rae is right. What do you think? <<> Senior Political Correspondent shy99@hani.co.kr (6·3 전국 동시 지방선거와 함께 치르는 국회의원 재보궐 선거의 열기가 지방선거 못지않게 뜨겁습니다. 그중에서도 가장 큰 관심이 쏠리는 곳은 부산 북갑입니다.)

item.title: 'Jung Cheong-rae Assassination Squad' Post Appears on SNS Group Chat… Democratic Party Requests Investigation (SNS 단체방에 ‘정청래 암살단’ 글 올라와…민주, 수사 의뢰)
item.description:
The Democratic Party of Korea announced on the 17th that it has received a tip about a planned terror attack targeting its leader, Jung Cheong-rae, ahead of the June 3 local elections, and has requested an investigation and personal protection from the police. (더불어민주당이 6·3 지방선거를 앞두고 정청래 대표에 대한 테러 모의가 있다는 제보가 접수돼 경찰에 수사를 의뢰하고 신변보호를 요청했다고 17일 밝혔다.)

Kang Jun-hyun, the senior spokesperson for the Democratic Party, held a press conference at the National Assembly on the same day, stating, "We have received consecutive tips that a group terror plot is being discussed on an unidentified SNS group chat," and added, "The party yesterday requested a swift investigation from the police and thorough personal protection." He further said, "Not only the act of terror itself but even plotting it constitutes a serious crime," and added, "If such plotting causes Representative Jung to shrink back in his activities, it amounts to political violence and intimidation against the future of South Korea." (강준현 민주당 수석대변인은 이날 국회에서 기자회견을 열어 “실체를 알 수 없는 에스엔에스(SNS) 단체방에서 집단 테러 모의가 이뤄지고 있다는 제보가 잇따라 접수됐다”며 “당 차원에서 어제 경찰에 신속 수사를 의뢰하고 철저한 신변 보호를 요청했다”고 말했다. 그는 “테러뿐만 아니라 테러 모의만으로도 중대범죄”라며 “이런 모의로 인해 정 대표 행보가 위축되면 이건 대한민국 미래에 가하는 정치적 폭력이자 협박”이라고 덧붙였다.)

Spokesperson Kang said, "Simply creating an atmosphere of fear that forces one to be cautious already qualifies as a serious obstruction of election activities," and stated, "Posts are currently appearing recruiting a 'Jung Cheong-rae assassination squad' and seeking membership in it. Concerning the suspicions of a terror plot, we urge the police to promptly initiate an investigation, including into those behind it." (강 수석대변인은 “공포심 때문에 몸 사릴 수밖에 없도록 만드는 것만으로도 이미 심각한 선거운동 방해 행위에 해당한다”며 “현재 정청래 암살단 모집과 그 암살단에 가입 신청한다는 글들이 올라오고 있으니 테러 모의 의혹과 관련해 그 배후를 포함해 신속한 수사 절차 개시를 경찰에 촉구한다”고 밝혔다.)

In response to a reporter's question about whether this is seen as organized plotting rather than a temporary outburst of anger, he answered, "From the party's perspective, it wasn't just a simple expression of opinion; specific expressions appeared, which led even to the request for an investigation." Regarding Representative Jung's future schedule, he said, "It will proceed as planned." (그는 ‘일시적 분노표출이 아닌 조직적 모의 정황으로 보고 있느냐’는 취재진 질문에 “(당에선) 단순한 의사 표현이 아니고 구체적인 표현까지 등장했기 때문에 수사 의뢰까지 진행하게 된 것”이라고 답했다. 정 대표 향후 일정과 관련해서는 “예정대로 진행한다”고 말했다.)

Meanwhile, Representative Jung posted on Facebook that day, mentioning that a police investigation had been requested regarding the terror plot, and said, "I hope we practice politics that saves lives, not politics that takes them," adding, "I will be more cautious, stay more humble, and work even harder." (한편 정 대표는 이날 페이스북에 글을 올려 테러 모의에 대한 경찰 수사 의뢰 사실을 언급하며 “사람을 죽이는 정치가 아니라 사람을 살리는 정치를 했으면 좋겠다”며 “더 조심하며 더 낮게 더 열심히 뛰겠다”고 밝혔다.)

By Ha Eo-young, Reporter haha@hani.co.kr (하어영 기자 haha@hani.co.kr)

item.title: Oh Se-hoon and Lee Jun-seok Join Hands to Meet Youth… "No Merger Under Review" (오세훈-이준석, 손잡고 청년 만나…“단일화는 검토 안해”)
item.description:
Oh Se-hoon, the People Power Party candidate for Seoul mayor, and Lee Jun-seok, leader of the Reform Party, visited the field together to launch a 'joint offensive' against the conservative camp. (오세훈 국민의힘 서울시장 후보가 이준석 개혁신당 대표와 함께 현장을 찾아 여권을 향한 ‘협공’에 나섰다.)

On the 16th, Candidate Oh, along with Leader Lee and Kim Jeong-cheol, the Reform Party's Seoul mayoral candidate, visited a studio apartment in Gongneung-dong, Nowon-gu, Seoul, and held an on-site meeting with a college student from a nearby university. (오 후보는 16일 이 대표, 김정철 개혁신당 서울시장 후보와 함께 서울 노원구 공릉동의 한 원룸을 방문해서 인근 대학에 다니는 한 청년과 현장 간담회를 가졌다.)

After the meeting, the first question from reporters who had been waiting was about 'electoral alliance.' In response, Leader Lee said, "Speaking as party leader, we are not considering candidate merger or electoral alliance," adding, "On policy matters, we share a common intent to check the monopoly of the Lee Jae-myung administration." (간담회가 끝난 뒤 기다리던 기자들의 첫 질문은 ‘선거 연대’ 여부였다. 이에 이 대표는 “당대표 입장에서 제가 말씀드리자면 저희는 뭐 후보 단일화나 선거 연대는 검토하고 있지 않다”며 “정책 관련 사안에 대해서는 이재명 정부의 독주에 대해서는 공통적으로 견제할 의사가 있다”고 말했다.)

Candidate Oh also said, "I fully agree (with Leader Lee's remarks)," and stated, "I believe it is very meaningful to unite efforts in solving the problems of those who suffer the most." Candidate Oh added, "We will focus on policy cooperation and strive to form a united front going forward with any party or faction that shares our intent." (오 후보 역시 “(이 대표 말에) 적극 동감이다”라며 “이런 가장 고통을 받는 분들의 문제를 해결함에 있어서 힘을 모으는 건 굉장히 의미가 크다고 생각한다”고 말했다. 오 후보는 “정책 연대에 대해서 중점을 둬서 앞으로도 어느 정당, 어느 정파라도 뜻을 함께한다면 함께하는 모습 만들어가도록 노력하겠다”고도 했다.)

During the on-site meeting, a college student living in the studio apartment voiced difficulties with housing issues. In response, Candidate Oh told the student, "The big problem is that if the current government's policies continue, rents and jeonse will rise further next year and the year after." He then mentioned his pledge to 'supply 74,000 homes for youth and newlyweds within four years' and added, "I'm not sure if it will work out as planned." (현장 간담회에서 원룸에 거주하는 한 대학생은 주거 문제의 어려움을 토로했다. 이에 오 후보는 대학생을 향해 “지금 큰일 난 게 이 정부 지금 정책대로 하면 내년 내후년에는 월세, 전세 더 오를 거다”라고 말했다. 이어 ‘청년·신혼부부 주택 4년 내 7만4천 호 공급’ 등 자신의 공약을 언급한 뒤 “뜻대로 될지 모르겠다”고 말하기도 했다.)

Later, Leader Lee told reporters, "The fact that opposition Seoul mayoral candidates came together today is due to a common recognition that the Lee Jae-myung administration's real estate policy is actually threatening the housing of the younger generation," and added, "The opposition camp is, in fact, very concerned about the current real estate policies of the Lee Jae-myung administration." (이 대표는 이후 기자들에게 “오늘 이렇게 야권의 서울시장 후보들이 함께한 것은 그만큼 이재명 정부의 부동산 정책이 실질적으로 젊은 세대의 주거를 위협하고 있다는 공통의 인식 때문”이라며 “야권에서는 사실 지금 이재명 정부의 부동산 정책에 대해서 굉장히 우려스러운 입장을 가지고 있다”고 했다.)

Candidate Oh argued, "We visited a young person's monthly rent room today. While we symbolically chose this location, the message we want to convey with our united hearts is that if the current administration's policy direction continues, phenomena like a surge in monthly rents within the next one or two years will make it nearly impossible to find a solution." (오 후보는 “오늘 한 젊은 청년의 월세 방을 방문했다. 상징적으로 이 장소를 선택하긴 했지만 오늘 저희가 마음을 모아서 전달해드리고 싶은 메시지는 앞으로 1, 2년 내에 월세 폭등 등의 현상이 현 정부의 정책 기조대로 가게 되면 해결될 실마리를 찾기가 불가능에 가깝다는 것”이라고 주장했다.)

Reporter Song Gyeong-hwa freehwa@hani.co.kr (송경화 기자 freehwa@hani.co.kr)

item.title: Hong Joon-pyo Says "Busan Buk-gu Gap 1st, 2nd, 3rd Place Is as Clear as Day"—Who Did He Predict Would Win? (홍준표 “부산북갑 1·2·3등 불 보듯 뻔해”…누구 당선 예측했나)
item.description:
Former Daegu Mayor Hong Joon-pyo, regarding the upcoming Busan Buk-gu Gap by-election for the National Assembly, stated that "the first, second, and third places are as clear as day," highly predicting the possibility of Ha Jung-woo, the Democratic Party of Korea candidate, winning. (홍준표 전 대구시장이 다가오는 부산 북갑 국회의원 보궐선거를 두고 “1·2·3등이 불 보듯 뻔하다”며 하정우 더불어민주당 후보 당선 가능성을 높게 점쳤다.)

In a video posted on his YouTube channel on the 16th, the former Mayor Hong said about the Busan Buk-gu Gap election, which will be held alongside the June 3 local elections, "The first, second, and third places are as clear as day," adding, "Especially because it's the electoral district of National Assembly member Jeon Jae-soo, who is running in the (Busan mayoral) local election, Jeon's influence will likely be extremely significant." He also stated, "Because Jeon Jae-soo is running for Busan mayor, there is concern that (Ha Jung-woo of the Democratic Party) might ride on Jeon's coattails." This analysis suggests that by evaluating the strong influence of candidate Jeon Jae-soo, a three-term lawmaker from the Busan Buk-gu Gap district, Ha Jung-woo's chances of winning are high. <<> Regarding the possibility of a merger between Park Min-shik, the People Power Party candidate running in Buk-gu Gap, and independent candidate Han Dong-hoon, Hong assessed it as unlikely. The former Mayor said, "There can be no merger," adding, "One is a person expelled for defamation crimes, and the other is someone who left Buk-gu and then returned; if they merge, the current People Power Party leadership would be contradicting themselves." He successively mentioned Candidate Han, who was expelled from the People Power Party in January amid suspicions that his family posted defamatory remarks about former President Yoon Suk-yeol and his wife on the party's bulletin board in 2024, and Candidate Park, who has a history of running in districts like Seoul Gangseo-eul in the 2024 general election. <<> Regarding the Seoul mayoral election, Hong said, "Looking at the opinion poll results, (the Democratic Party's candidate Jung Won-oh) was overwhelmingly leading due to the president's halo and the administration's halo, but recent polls have narrowed the gap." He added, "Whether Mayor Oh Se-hoon will achieve the feat of a fifth term in the history of popularly elected local government heads, or whether a Seoul mayor from a district office chief background will emerge based on the achievements of the Seongdong-gu office chief, I don't know how Seoul citizens will decide, but looking at the situation so far, it seems Mayor Oh is campaigning in a atmosphere of chasing from behind. This might be a first for Mayor Oh." <<> Concerning the Busan mayoral election, Hong commented, "In Busan mayoral elections, the People Power Party has always stood as the defender, and the Democratic Party as the challenger, but this time, interestingly, their positions seem to have switched." He said, "Rather, it appears candidate Jeon Jae-soo is taking the defender's position, while current Busan Mayor Park Hyung-joon is taking the attacker's position in the election." He added, "After the impeachment of Park Geun-hye, Busan had a Democratic Party mayor. This time, after the impeachment of Yoon Suk-yeol, we'll have to see if another Democratic Party mayor emerges, but Busan, unlike the TK (Daegu-Gyeongbuk) region, is a swing vote area," stating, "It's a region that can support the Democratic Party at any time." <<> Evaluating the Daegu mayoral election, Hong said, "A strong 'Kim Boo-kyum wind' is blowing," and described it as "an election to choose who will realize and complete the TK new airport." Previously, the former Mayor Hong had cited Democratic Party candidate Kim Boo-kyum as a suitable figure for the next Daegu mayor in April. <<> Regarding the overall trend of the June 3 local elections, Former Mayor Hong assessed, "The Seoul and Busan elections were conditions where the Democratic Party could easily win, but the fact that the gap has narrowed is due to the stance of the ruling party in power that committed the stupid act of the 'withdrawal of indictment special counsel.'" He added, "It would have been fine to resolve the (trial issue) after (President Lee Jae-myung) left office, but by hastily trying to settle it while in office and causing a stir ahead of the elections, they made what could have been a smooth election in Seoul and Busan very difficult." He also said, "For elections in other regions (excluding Seoul, Busan, and Daegu), I think most outcomes are already decided, except for Ulsan region, even without me specifically mentioning it." <<> Reporter Jeon Gwang-jun light@hani.co.kr (홍 전 시장은 16일 자신의 유튜브 채널에 올린 영상에서 6·3 지방선거에서 함께 치러질 부산 북갑 선거를 두고 “1·2·3등이 불 보듯이 뻔하다”며 “특히 (부산시장) 지방선거에 나온 전재수 국회의원의 선거구이기 때문에 아마 전재수의 영향력이 굉장히 클 것”이라고 말했다. “전재수가 부산시장으로 나왔기 때문에 전재수에 (하정우 더불어민주당 후보가) 묻어갈 우려도 있다”고도 했다. 부산 북갑을 지역구로 3선 의원을 지낸 전재수 후보 영향력이 크다고 평가하면서 하정우 후보 당선 가능성이 크다는 식으로 분석한 것이다.)

item.title: PM Kim: "Regarding Samsung Electronics Strike, We Will Pursue All Measures Including Emergency Mediation" (김 총리 “삼성전자 파업, 긴급조정 포함 모든 대응 강구”)
item.description:
Prime Minister Kim Min-seok stated on the 17th regarding the labor-management conflict at Samsung Electronics over performance bonuses, "If a situation arises where the strike causes significant damage to the national economy, the government must consider all possible response measures, including emergency mediation, to protect the national economy." (김민석 국무총리가 17일 성과급을 둘러싼 삼성전자 노사 갈등과 관련해 “파업으로 국민경제에 막대한 피해가 우려되는 상황이 발생한다면 정부는 국민 경제 보호를 위해 긴급조정을 포함한 가능한 모든 대응 수단을 강구하지 않을 수 없다”라고 말했다.)

Prime Minister Kim made these remarks during a 'Public Address on the Samsung Electronics Strike' at the Joint Press Briefing Room of the Seoul Government Complex. He added, "The solution to labor-management issues should be found not through confrontation and conflict, but through dialogue based on trust and responsible consultation. The government will actively support dialogue between labor and management up to the very end to prevent a strike under any circumstances." (김 총리는 이날 정부서울청사 합동브리핑실에서 ‘삼성전자 파업 관련 대국민담화’를 통해 이렇게 말했다. 김 총리는 “노사 문제의 해법은 대립과 충돌이 아니라 신뢰에 기반한 대화와 책임있는 협의를 통해 마련돼야 할 것”이라며 “정부는 그 어떠한 경우에도 파업으로 이어지지 않게끔 노사 간의 대화를 끝까지 적극 지원하겠다”고 했다.)

The emergency mediation authority is a power that the Minister of Employment and Labor can invoke when a strike is likely to cause significant harm to the national economy or daily life. If the emergency mediation authority is invoked, the labor union must cease all industrial actions for 30 days, and the government will engage in mediation and arbitration during that period. The Ministry of Employment and Labor, as the responsible ministry, has maintained the position that it has not yet conducted a practical review of the requirements for invoking the emergency mediation authority. With Samsung Electronics' labor and management set to hold a second post-mediation meeting on the morning of the 18th at the Central Labor Relations Commission in Sejong City, Prime Minister Kim urged, "I sincerely request, together with all citizens, that labor and management achieve results in tomorrow's post-mediation meeting, which is effectively the last opportunity." <<> By Jeong Hye-min, Reporter jhm@hani.co.kr (긴급조정권은 파업이 국민경제나 일상에 큰 피해를 줄 우려가 있을 때 고용노동부 장관이 발동할 수 있는 권한이다. 긴급조정권이 발동되면 노동조합은 30일 동안 모든 쟁의행위를 중단해야 하고, 정부는 그 기간에 조정과 중재에 나서게 된다. 주무부처인 고용노동부는 긴급조정권 발동 요건을 실무적으로 검토한 바 없다는 입장을 고수해왔다. 삼성전자 노사가 오는 18일 오전 세종시 중앙노동위원회에서 2차 사후조정 회의를 열 예정인 가운데, 김 총리는 “사실상 마지막 기회인 내일 사후조정에서 노사가 반드시 성과를 내주시기를 온 국민과 함께 간절히 요청드린다”라고 당부했다. )
